If the drainage area above a detention structure is a significant percentage of the total drainage area contributing to downstream flooding, then the downstream area should experience reduced flooding due to flood flow regulation. When spillway discharges are required, the effectiveness of flood regulation steadily decreases with increased flood severity. In the unlikely event of failure of the dam, a mass of water would surge downstream, carrying debris and sediment and causing unusually high flood stages. It must be emphasized though, that the probability of such an event is quite low, and that due to the relatively small size of tributary impoundments, downstream effects would be minimal.
The removal of aquifers in the coal seams and in overburden and interburden will result in temporary reductions or interruptions of springflow. Springs originating from the overburden, Rosebud-McKay coal and interburden may be permanently lost. Such losses are not of great concern since these springs are largely intermittent. Increased infiltration and permeability of the reclaimed aquifer will result in some locally increased springflow into adjacent watersheds after mining is completed. This will be particularly true for Tract III along Middle Fork Sarpy and East Fork Sarpy Creeks, however, the increase is not expected to significantly add to the overall surface flow volume.
